newsitem.title: UK: UK RPIX target of 2.5 pct "sensible" - Labour aide.
newsitem.headline: UK RPIX target of 2.5 pct "sensible" - Labour aide.

text.p: Ed Balls, a leading adviser to UK opposition Labour's finance spokesman Gordon Brown, told reporters on Monday that an inflation target of 2.5 percent for the medium term was a sensible objective.
"2.5 percent or less in the medium term would be a sensible objective," he said.
He echoed comments made by Brown at the CBI annual conference that Labour would not just talk tough on inflation, but would also deliver on its target.
Balls said the Labour Party had not yet made a decision on the precise wording of its inflation target.
"We won't make an announcement until we have consulted with the Bank of England," he said.
He was referring to underlying inflation, RPIX, which strips out volatile mortgage interest payments.
The Conservative government has a 2.5 percent inflation target. RPIX edged up to 2.9 percent in September.
